reuse.why: Builds on the existing link.ts guards, but the new unlinkLocalAccount re-writes the column reset of unlinkAccount instead of extracting it so unlinkAccount uses it too.

duplication.why: The same five-line 'assert, and if a replaced id comes back unlink it' block is pasted into all six provider link functions, and unlinkLocalAccount copies unlinkAccount's update block.

placement.why: The takeover helpers live in accounts/link.ts beside the existing link guards, which is the right module; the orchestration is spread over provider functions because the tree has no common link path.

scope.why: Only the flag, its handling and focused tests; nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: An 'assert' function that now conditionally returns an id is a confusing contract, and the six copied takeover blocks plus two copies of the unlink reset must all be kept in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Uses the existing link.ts guards; unlinkAccount is a request handler that would contact the provider, so not calling it is defensible, though its reset was copied rather than shared.

disguised_duplication.where: unlinkLocalAccount is a verbatim copy of unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount block, and the per-provider takeover blocks are identical copies; neither is disguised.
